createdFor: Clarity role-play walkthrough and utilization-review training
guardrails: No real PHI, no real police report, no real facility data.
Diagnoses are provisional training drafts and require clinician review.
Legal status and hold language are placeholders and require counsel validation.
Utilization-review language is a draft support summary, not payer authorization or medical-necessity certification.

patients.referralSource: Brooklyn 99 field welfare check by Amy Santiago and Terry Jeffords
patients.assignedStaff: Pam Beesly intake, Jim Halpert clinician review, Oscar Martinez UR
provisionalDiagnoses: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe, with anxious distress
patients.precipitatingEvents: After an abrupt retirement-board conflict and perceived public humiliation, patient sent multiple goodbye-style texts, stopped eating for two days, and was found pacing near a bridge with disorganized paperwork and no clear plan for safe return home.
patients.riskSummary: High danger-to-self concern due to goodbye texts, impaired sleep/appetite, hopeless statements, and unsafe location. No homicidal ideation reported. Medical comorbidities require medication reconciliation.
patients.recommendedDisposition: Inpatient psychiatric admission, voluntary if capacity and consent confirmed; otherwise legal-status review required.
patients.urDecision: Draft supports acute inpatient level of care due to imminent safety concern, functional decline, need for 24-hour monitoring, medication reconciliation, and failure of outpatient coping supports.

patients.insurance: Original Medicare Part A/B with supplemental policy
patients.referralSource: Brooklyn 99 field response by Rosa Diaz and Raymond Holt
patients.assignedStaff: Michael Scott intake director, Phyllis Vance charge nurse, Angela Martin compliance
provisionalDiagnoses: Bipolar I disorder, current episode manic, severe, without psychotic features
patients.precipitatingEvents: Neighbors reported three nights of no sleep, loud property destruction, and patient attempting to leave town with firearms despite chest pain complaints and missed diabetes medication.
patients.riskSummary: High risk of accidental harm and impaired judgment. Medical risk elevated by diabetes, chest pain history, possible alcohol withdrawal, and firearm access. No direct suicidal intent documented.
patients.recommendedDisposition: Medical clearance followed by inpatient psychiatric admission with safety precautions and restricted access to weapons.
patients.urDecision: Draft supports acute inpatient level of care due to severe mania, impaired judgment, unsafe behavior, need for medication stabilization, withdrawal monitoring, and medical comorbidity coordination.

patients.insurance: Medicare due disability with Medicaid secondary
patients.referralSource: Brooklyn 99 transport request by Charles Boyle and Jake Peralta
patients.assignedStaff: Pam Beesly intake, Jim Halpert clinician review, Oscar Martinez UR
patients.precipitatingEvents: Patient reported escalating panic, insomnia, and trauma flashbacks after a motor vehicle crash anniversary. Family collateral described medication overuse concern and inability to complete basic self-care for three days.
patients.riskSummary: Moderate-to-high self-neglect and medication safety risk. Passive death wishes reported without active plan. Chronic pain and sleep apnea complicate sedating-medication decisions.
patients.recommendedDisposition: Inpatient psychiatric admission for stabilization, medication safety, and trauma-informed safety planning after medical review.
patients.urDecision: Draft supports inpatient level of care due to impaired self-care, medication overuse concern, persistent trauma symptoms, inability to stabilize with family support, and need for 24-hour observation.

patients.referralSource: Brooklyn 99 response by Rosa Diaz after workplace concern
patients.assignedStaff: Jim Halpert clinician review, Angela Martin compliance, Oscar Martinez UR
provisionalDiagnoses: Rule out borderline personality disorder traits
patients.precipitatingEvents: Coworkers reported patient posted cryptic farewell messages, gave away personal items, and was found in a locked supply room with superficial cuts and refusal to contract for safety.
patients.riskSummary: Imminent self-harm concern with recent self-injury, farewell messaging, concealment, and inability to collaborate on safety planning.
patients.recommendedDisposition: Inpatient psychiatric admission with suicide precautions and clinician review for voluntary vs involuntary status.
patients.urDecision: Draft supports acute inpatient level of care due to recent self-injury, inability to maintain safety at lower level, need for close observation, and active treatment planning.

patients.referralSource: Brooklyn 99 response by Jake Peralta and Charles Boyle
patients.assignedStaff: Michael Scott intake director, Pam Beesly intake, Phyllis Vance charge nurse
patients.precipitatingEvents: Patient was found wandering in traffic, singing loudly, responding to unseen stimuli, and stating he had been chosen to stop an invisible emergency. Collateral reported medication nonadherence for two weeks.
patients.riskSummary: High grave-disability and accidental-harm risk due to psychosis, traffic exposure, impaired judgment, and medication nonadherence. No intentional violence reported.
patients.recommendedDisposition: Inpatient psychiatric admission after medical clearance, elopement precautions, and restart/stabilization of psychiatric medication.
patients.urDecision: Draft supports inpatient level of care due to psychosis, inability to maintain personal safety, failed outpatient adherence, and need for 24-hour structured medication stabilization.

patients.referralSource: Brooklyn 99 response by Amy Santiago and Terry Jeffords
patients.assignedStaff: Pam Beesly intake, Oscar Martinez UR, Angela Martin compliance
provisionalDiagnoses: Stimulant use disorder, mild to moderate
patients.precipitatingEvents: Patient presented to ED with chest tightness, panic, pressured speech, and escalating paranoid fear after several days of stimulant misuse and no sleep. He attempted to leave before medical clearance.
patients.riskSummary: Moderate medical and behavioral risk due to chest-pain presentation, stimulant misuse, hypertension, insomnia, and elopement attempt before clearance.
patients.recommendedDisposition: Dual medical-behavioral review; inpatient psychiatric admission if medically cleared and unable to maintain safety at crisis-stabilization level.
patients.urDecision: Draft supports inpatient psychiatric admission if medical clearance confirms behavioral-health primary need, due to elopement risk, impaired judgment, stimulant-related instability, and failed ED de-escalation.
